comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 regulations and exact Dutch prospectus establish 180 EC. The first year contains twelve required 5 EC courses. The later years contain nine required 5 EC courses and the 15 EC Bachelor Project. At least 20 EC of specialisation and enough Psychology electives to reach 30 EC are required, alongside 30 EC of open study in this illustration. Both selected specialisation courses require passing all first-year courses. The standard Bachelor Project requires passing year one and Multivariate Data Analysis. Students work in a research team and are assessed on a research article, presentation and the research and collaboration process.

alternatives.label: Psychology, behavior and research methods
alternatives.concept: Study how people think, develop and behave in social and clinical settings. Connect lifespan development, cognition and psychopathology with psychological assessment and research. Use experiments, qualitative inquiry, evidence synthesis and econometrics to study behavior from several perspectives.
progression: Brain & Behavior precedes advanced psychology and cognition. Statistics & Experimental Methods precedes evidence synthesis. Research Methods & Statistics precedes econometrics.
alternatives.labelReason: The broad option combines psychological study across domains with a sequence in several research methods.

alternatives.label: Brain and cognition
alternatives.concept: Study how the brain supports perception, action, memory and language. Use neurobiology and life science to connect neural processes with behavior, and develop complementary skills in behavioral experiments, data analysis and computational vision.
alternatives.distinctness: The brain and cognition option adds a life science gateway, physiology, anatomy, molecular study, laboratory work and computational data analysis.
progression: The two gateways precede advanced cognition and life science. Introduction to Data Science precedes Machine Learning and computer vision. Experimental methods and statistical analysis support later evidence synthesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Neurobiology, perception, language and higher cognition organize this option; life science and data methods support it.

alternatives.label: Psychology, leadership and organizations
alternatives.concept: Study how people make decisions, cooperate and respond to leadership. Combine social and organizational psychology with communication, negotiation and behavioral economics. Use market research and quantitative and qualitative methods to investigate questions about people in organizations.
alternatives.labelReason: Organizational psychology, leadership, negotiation and behavioral decision-making organize this option.
alternatives.distinctness: The organizational option adds business foundations, leadership practice, negotiation, market research, consumer engagement and behavioral economics.
progression: Entrepreneurship and research foundations precede market research, organizational psychology, negotiation and behavioral economics. Introductory leadership precedes communication and applied work.

candidates.label: A brain and cognition route centred on cognitive neuroscience, perception, learning, memory and language.
A social and organisational psychology route centred on social influence, groups, organisations, leadership and applied behavioural research.
A clinical-psychology and mental-health direction centred on psychological problems, clinical psychology and health.
candidates.reason: The broad option already includes psychopathology, assessment, health psychology and development. A separate clinical option would either repeat those courses or imply a more extensive clinical training sequence.

candidates.label: A development, trauma and child-abuse direction spanning the lifespan.
candidates.reason: Developmental psychology, psychopathology and youth resilience support parts of the direction. The broad option covers these interests, while specialist child abuse and neglect coursework remains a gap.

routeSelection.route: Dutch-taught Psychology with Cognitive Neuroscience and Social Psychology in Organisations
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Psychology bachelor. The programme requires specialisation choices but is explicitly broad. Selecting one cognitive-neuroscience course and one social-organisational course preserves that cross-domain identity and avoids presenting a narrow clinical, cognitive or organisational profile as the whole programme. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad option covers development, clinical and social psychology, cognition and behavioral methods. The brain option adds biological mechanisms, laboratory work and computation. The organizational option adds applied leadership, consumer behavior and organizational research. The clinical and development/trauma interests are visible within the broad option; separate professional clinical or specialist trauma curricula would overstate the depth of the available sequence.

notes.text: Leiden requires dedicated psychometrics and interpersonal professional skills, two specialisation courses in this plan, and a 15 EC psychology research project. UCR includes related assessment, methods and psychology courses. Optional UCR independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Psychology bachelor studies behavior, cognition, development and mental health. Students learn psychological research methods, take specialisation courses and complete a supervised research project. This comparison uses the Dutch-taught route.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR options emphasize broad psychology and research, brain and cognition, or psychology and organizations. Each brings together psychology and complementary disciplines. Leiden provides a more extensive sequence of psychology-specific measurement and professional skills.
